# `minimum-decreased`

minimum decreased

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `info` in requests, `warn` in responses |
| **Rule IDs** | `minimum-decreased` (both directions), `minimum-decreased-in-request`, `minimum-decreased-in-response` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M5) |
| **Group** | Schemas ([RULES.md section 7](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

`minimum` or `exclusiveMinimum` decreased.

## Why this default

In requests: more numbers are valid. In responses: clients may receive values (e.g. negatives) they do not expect.

## Example

From test case [`minimum-decreased`](../../test/cases/minimum-decreased/): minimum lowered on a response number.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
          name:
            type: integer
-           minimum: 1
+           minimum: 0
```

Findings:

- `minimum-decreased-in-response` · warn · #/components/schemas/Pet

## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  minimum-decreased: warn
```

## How to fix

Check that clients handle the smaller values.
